title: TagDuel concession transaction rollback under SQLite write faults
scenarios: A SQLite trigger aborts the transition-event insert during quitTag from an inactive teammate. The terminal status, winner, revision, serialized state and all four participant locks must remain unchanged; retry after dropping the trigger must finish the duel and release all four locks exactly once.

A SQLite trigger aborts lock deletion after quitTag has updated the terminal row and inserted its event. The entire transaction must roll back; retry must persist one terminal event, the opposite team as winner, and zero remaining locks.
invariants: Any physical teammate may concede for their team, including the inactive partner.
Terminal session state, winner, revision, transition event and participant lock release commit or roll back together.
Failed termination does not consume or duplicate physical card UIDs.
Player rows and player_cards remain unchanged.
Retry after a transient SQLite failure uses the original revision and produces exactly one terminal transition.
limits: Tests use temporary SQLite and the real compiled TagStore/TagDuel modules.
Fault injection covers SQL trigger aborts, not process termination or filesystem corruption.
No runtime, resolver, catalog manifest, allowlist, persistent database or player data is modified.
This is a TagDuel persistence regression and certifies no new card behavior.
No live Discord API session is performed.
command: npm run check && npm run build && node --test tests/tagQuitRollbackAtomicity2v2.test.cjs
